'''''Festuca incurva''''' is a [[species]] of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Poaceae]], [[Native species|native]] from the [[Mediterranean Basin|Mediterranean]] to Central Asia and [[Pakistan]].<ref name=POWO_77144481-1/> When placed in the [[Monotypic taxon|monotypic]] [[genus]] '''''Psilurus''''' as '''''Psilurus incurvus''''', it was the only species.<ref name=POWO_Psilurus/>

==Taxonomy==
The species was first described by [[Antoine Gouan]] in 1762 as ''Nardus incurva''.<ref name=IPNI_77144481-1/> In 1913, it was transferred to the genus ''Psilurus'' as the only species ''Psilurus incurvus''. In 2014, it was transferred to ''Festuca'', the placement accepted by [[Plants of the World Online]] {{as of|lc=yes|2024|11}}.<ref name=POWO_77144481-1/>

==Distribution==
''Festuca incurva'' has a widespread distribution. It is native to southwestern Europe (the [[Balearic Islands]], [[Corsica]], France, Portugal, [[Sardinia]] and Spain), southeastern Europe ([[Albania]], [[Bulgaria]], Greece, Italy, [[Crete]], [[Romania]], [[Sicily]], [[East Thrace|European Turkey]] and the former [[Yugoslavia]]), North Africa ([[Algeria]], [[Libya]], [[Morocco]], [[Tunisia]]), Western Asia ([[Afghanistan]], [[Cyprus]], the East Aegean Islands, [[Iran]], [[Iraq]], [[Lebanon]]-[[Syria]], [[Palestine (region)|Palestine]] and [[Turkey]]), the [[Caucasus]], [[Crimea]], [[Pakistan]], and Central Asia ([[Tajikistan]] and [[Uzbekistan]]). It has been introduced into Germany and parts of Australia.<ref name=POWO_77144481-1/>
